Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our procurement team reviewed the draft and had two items they want clarified before we take this to legal: the end-of-term reconciliation cadence for annual true-ups across a multi-year prepay, and how the buffer band interacts with tiered discounts/ramp.

Concretely: if ACME prepays Year 1 and Year 2 in advance, but usage in Year 2 spikes above the committed ramp, do we reconcile annually only (end of each 12 months) or at the end of the full term? Also, your team suggested a 10% buffer band — how does that apply to tiered overage rates vs. the prepay bucket?

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage file. I recommend the following operational approach (high level) that balances predictability for Acme and accounting simplicity for both sides: 

1) Annual reconciliation windows: we perform reconciliations at the end of each 12-month anniversary. That gives both teams a yearly true-up (credit or invoice) and avoids a single large reconciliation at year 3 that can create forecasting headaches.

2) Multi-year committed ramp: each year in the multi-year contract has an explicit committed volume. Example: Year 1 = 100M tokens, Year 2 = 150M tokens, Year 3 = 200M tokens. The ramp is baked into the prepay schedule and associated discount schedule.

3) Buffer band application: the buffer band (we typically propose 10%) is applied at the annual reconciliation level. If actual usage for the anniversary year is within +/-10% of the committed volume for that year, no charge/credit is applied (this avoids churn on minor forecasting variance). When usage exceeds committed + buffer band, the overage is billed at the overage rate associated with the tier that the excess volume falls into.

4) Cumulative true-up cap: to address Acme's concern about spikes, we can add a safety cap that no single anniversary true-up charge will exceed 50% of that year’s prepay amount — excess is carried to the next anniversary and reconciled then. This smooths cash flow volatility while preserving Redwood's economics.

5) Reporting & disputes: we provide a detailed per-route usage export and a reconciliation summary within 10 business days of the anniversary. Any dispute window is 30 days with supporting logs.

I'll loop in Vanessa (discounts) and Rishi (finance) to confirm the discount interaction and legal-visible wording. If you want, I can convert the above into Appendix A for the contract.

Cheers,
Lauren

Lauren / team — quick notes from a pricing perspective:

- Tiered discounts should be applied to the committed prepay buckets first, then overage pricing applies to any usage beyond committed + buffer. In practice that means overage rates are higher than the marginal prepay-equivalent rate (we can show numeric examples).
- For multi-year deals where the customer prepays multiple years up-front, we will honor the discount schedule locked-in at signature for the committed volumes. If Acme prepays Years 1+2 now and usage surges in Year 2, the excess that becomes overage is billed at the overage schedule for Year 2 (not at Year 3 pricing) — unless both parties agree to a restructured amendment.
- The 50% single-anniversary cap Lauren proposed is acceptable for strategic customers but should be limited to Enterprise SAAS deals and negotiated at the ACV tier level.

I can prepare a small appendix with worked examples (Year-by-year tables) — recommend we attach that to the contract as Appendix A.

V.

Tom — short answer: yes, Redwood can issue a credit memo against the original prepay invoice. Operational details:

- We generate either an overage invoice or a credit memo at the anniversary true-up. Credits are applied to the next Redwood invoice by default; if the customer prefers a refund (bank transfer), we can accommodate subject to finance review.
- We'll add language to Appendix A that credits will either be applied in the next invoice cycle or refunded on request (refunds take up to 30 days to process).
- On the mechanistic side, our billing system references the prepay invoice ID and attaches the credit memo for auditability — we can provide sample invoice/credit numbers to Acme accounting when we send the first reconciliation.

I'll prepare the 2 worked examples Vanessa mentioned and a short paragraph showing how the buffer band maps to numerical outcomes. Lauren — want me to push the Appendix A draft to Drive so Acme can preview?
